title: Zachman and an overview of the classic frameworks

videos.script: In 1987, John Zachman asked a simple question. How do the people who build aeroplanes and buildings describe what they build? {{title}} His answer was that they never use one drawing. The owner, the architect and the builder each need their own, and each drawing answers one plain question. What. How. Where. Who. When. Why. {{questions}} Put the questions across the top and the people down the side, and you get a grid of thirty-six cells. {{grid}} That grid is the Zachman Framework. It is not a method. It tells you nothing about what to do next. It tells you what kind of description you are holding, and which ones are missing. {{ontology}} This lesson places every diagram of this course in that grid. Then it lines up all the classic frameworks side by side, so you can tell what each one actually is.
